title: Ear-EEG motor execution dataset from Wu et al 2020
description: This dataset comprises ear-EEG recordings from six healthy participants performing motor execution tasks (fist clenching) with simultaneous scalp and ear-based EEG acquisition. The study includes 1,114 trials of left and right hand motor imagery cued by visual and auditory stimuli, sampled at 1000 Hz across 122 scalp channels. The dataset serves as a benchmark for motor task classification and brain-computer interface applications using in-ear sensing technology.
methods_description: Motor execution data were collected using Neuroscan SynAmps2 hardware with 122 EEG channels (Ag/AgCl sensors) and 10 miscellaneous channels, sampled at 1000 Hz with online bandpass filtering (0.5-100 Hz). Participants performed motor execution tasks (fist clenching) in response to visual and auditory arrow cues indicating left or right hand movements. Scalp reference and ground electrodes were used with standard 1005 montage.
